passages.title: Joshua receives the charge
passages.summary: Joshua succeeds Moses. Israel prepares to cross the Jordan, and the eastern tribes promise to help. Joshua must follow God’s law while leading the people. The eastern tribes must help their neighbors.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: The Church lesson connects courage with God’s presence and repeated scripture study.

passages.title: Rahab protects the spies
passages.summary: Two spies enter Jericho. Rahab hides them and obtains a promise to protect her household. A woman described as a prostitute acts decisively for her household. Later biblical writers recognize both her faith and her actions.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies Rahab as an example of faith expressed through action.

passages.title: Crossing the Jordan
passages.summary: The priests carry the ark into the Jordan. The account describes the waters stopping while Israel crosses. The crossing establishes Joshua’s authority through a pattern that recalls Moses. No exact crossing point is securely identified here.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: The Church lesson connects the crossing with trust in Christ and the promise of baptism.

passages.title: Stones for remembrance
passages.summary: Twelve representatives take stones from the Jordan. Israel camps at Gilgal and prepares to explain the memorial to children. The stones help children ask about the crossing. Parents must tell them what happened.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me asks readers to recognize God’s help and teach the next generation.

passages.title: Passover and the commander
passages.summary: Israel renews circumcision and observes Passover. Manna ends. Joshua encounters the commander of the Lord’s army near Jericho. Israel keeps Passover and eats food from the land. The manna ends as life changes.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: The older manual proposes that the commander may be the Lord. It acknowledges the limited details.

passages.title: Jericho and Rahab’s rescue
passages.summary: The account describes Jericho’s walls falling after a ritual march. Israel destroys the city but preserves Rahab and her household. Israel destroys Jericho but keeps its promise to Rahab. Her household survives.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies trust and obedience through the account of Jericho.

passages.title: Achan and defeat at Ai
passages.summary: Israel loses at Ai. Achan admits taking forbidden goods. The account ends with the destruction of his household and possessions. The story connects individual wrongdoing with collective disaster. The severe punishment is part of its ancient setting.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies how Achan's hidden choice harms other people.

passages.title: Ai and the law at Ebal
passages.summary: Joshua captures Ai through an ambush. He then builds an altar on Ebal and reads the law before the assembly. Victory at Ai leads to a public reading of the law. Both children and strangers hear it.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: The manual connects the public reading with Moses's instructions. Who hears the people's promise?

passages.title: The Gibeonite agreement
passages.summary: Gibeonite envoys disguise their nearby origin. Israel swears an oath, then assigns them forced labor after discovering the deception. Israel's leaders keep their oath to spare Gibeon. They assign its people work carrying water and wood.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: The older Church manual studies keeping a promise when its cost becomes clear.

passages.title: The southern coalition
passages.summary: Five kings attack Gibeon. Joshua comes to its aid. The account describes hail, an extended day, and southern campaigns. Joshua answers Gibeon’s call for help. The chapter includes a poem about the sun and moon.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show named places and approximate regions. They do not establish exact campaign roads, tribal boundaries, or the date of a conquest.

lds.text: The older Church manual compares the long day with Helaman 12.

passages.title: Joshua’s farewell warning
passages.summary: Joshua warns Israel’s leaders about worshiping other gods. He urges them to keep God’s covenant. The farewell acknowledges neighboring peoples still present. Its separation commands belong to this ancient covenant setting.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies Joshua’s final counsel and choosing to remain faithful to God.

guides.title: Study Joshua
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: Joshua receives the charge
steps.text: Joshua succeeds Moses. Israel prepares to cross the Jordan, and the eastern tribes promise to help. Joshua must follow God’s law while leading the people. The eastern tribes must help their neighbors.

steps.title: Remaining land and eastern inheritance
steps.text: Joshua is old, and land remains to be possessed. The chapter records eastern inheritances and recalls Balaam’s death. Joshua grows old while much land remains unclaimed. The tribes still have work ahead.

steps.title: The covenant at Shechem
steps.text: Joshua recalls the ancestors and Israel’s journey. The people renew the covenant. The book records Joshua’s death and the burials of Joseph and Eleazar. Joshua recalls God's help and asks the people to choose. Their promise becomes part of shared memory.
